WoW: Forever · Updated November 13, 2026 · Client build 1.60.1.70938 · Null Ossuary

Written for the live game, levels 1 to 60. Mechanics come from Blizzard's posts and the launch client with its hotfixes through November 12. Trained levels are foreverchanges.pro's reading of the client. Talent builds on the spec pages are Icy Veins' and Wowhead's published ones, each named and dated. Tactics past level 30 lean on WoWSims, a model, which has fitted Hunter shots and pets to combat logs at levels 34 to 48. No raid opens until December 9, so nothing here rests on raid logs. Legacy's TalentedTalentedTalentCastInstantYou gain talent points every level starting at level 5 instead of starting at level 10, but you still may not have more than 51 total talent points. perk starts talent points at level 5 instead of 10, with the same 51 total, so a character with it reaches each talent five levels sooner than the levels printed here. Where a hover tooltip and the text disagree, believe the text: tooltips can lag a hotfix.

Each spec page carries its own builds and rotation.

Dual Specialization opens at level 40, per Blizzard. Wowhead reports it is bought from the class trainer for 50 gold.

Blizzard frames the three trees as a spectrum. A Hunter can "double down on ... ranged combat and their pets, choose not to have a pet at all, or ... dance back and forth between ranged and melee combat."

Is Hunter for you?

Play Hunter if you want the pet, not you, holding the enemy, and you do not mind managing ammunition, a quiver and pet food.

Blizzard's own framing of the class: Hunters have "an amazing toolkit of problem-solving Aspects and attacks but cannot Stun or Interrupt," and in solo or small-group play the pet does the tanking.

Strengths

  • Blizzard credits the class with "an amazing toolkit of problem-solving Aspects and attacks"
  • Your pet holds the enemy, so you take very little damage
  • Ranged attacks take no glancing blows, which Wowhead gives as the reason Hunters can fight enemies above their level

Weaknesses

  • Ammunition, a quiver and pet food all cost bag space and money
  • An 8-yard minimum range you cannot shoot inside, which Forever did not remove
  • No Stun and no Interrupt in the trained kit, which Blizzard states as a limit of the class. Talents add some control later: IntimidationIntimidationTalentCastInstantCost8% of base ManaRange100 yd rangeCooldown60 sec cooldownDuration15 secCommand your pet to Stun the target for 3 sec on its next successful attack, which also gains 100% increased critical strike chance. Generates high threat. (pet stun) and Scatter ShotScatter ShotTalentCastInstantCost8% of base ManaRange15 yd rangeCooldown30 sec cooldownDuration4 secA short-range shot that deals 50% weapon damage and disorients the target for 4 sec. Any damage caused will remove the effect. Turns off your attack when used. (disorient)

New to this class?

Is the rotation simple? Yes. Mark, send the pet, sting, shoot. Each spec adds one or two buttons past level 25.

Is it forgiving? Solo, your pet holds the target. In a dungeon the pet is not the tank, so that cover is gone.

What carries you while levelling? Your pet tanks for you from level 10.

Does it need a group? No, solo the pet does the tanking.

Which race

Race is the smallest of the choices on this page, well behind spec, gear and knowing your rotation, and no race is a wrong answer for levelling (ours, not a source's).

Racials decide things in PvP, specifically the ones that break crowd control: Will to SurviveWill to SurviveTalentCastInstantCooldown180 sec cooldownInstantly removes all Stun effects. (Human, removes all stuns), Shatter CurseShatter CurseTalentCastInstantCooldown180 sec cooldownDuration8 secInstantly removes all Curses and Banes, and reduces all Magical damage taken by 5% for 8 sec. (Orc, removes Curses and Banes) and StoneformStoneformTalentCastInstantCooldown180 sec cooldownDuration8 secInstantly removes and grants immunity to all Bleed, Poison, and Disease effects, and reduces all Physical damage taken by 10% for 8 sec. Quality of life

  • Level 10 is the class. Do the pet chain the moment you reach it. Tame BeastTame BeastSpell · NatureCastInstantCost60% of base ManaRange30 yd rangeDuration20 secBegins taming a beast to be your companion. Your armor is reduced by 100% while you focus on taming the beast for 20 sec. If you lose the beast's attention for any reason, the taming process will fail. Once tamed, the beast will be very unhappy and disloyal. Try feeding the pet immediately to make it happy. does not work on beasts above your own level.
  • Ammunition and the quiver are real costs. The quiver gives a ranged attack-speed bonus and does not stack, so carry exactly one. Buy ammunition in stacks whenever you pass a vendor. Wowhead notes that Engineers craft the best ammunition in the game.
  • Aspect of the CheetahAspect of the CheetahLevel 20 · Spell · NatureCastInstantCost40 ManaDurationUntil cancelledThe hunter takes on the aspects of a cheetah, increasing movement speed by 30%. If the hunter takes damage, he will be dazed for 4 sec. Only one Aspect can be active at a time. is your mount until 40 and should be up almost all the time in the world; PathfindingPathfindingTalent · Rank 2 of 2CastInstantIncreases the speed bonus of your Aspect of the Cheetah and Aspect of the Pack by 6%. pushes it to +36%.   • Mail opens at 40, and a weapon master teaches anything you did not start with, including polearms from 20.
  • Train what you use. Whether a family still changes a pet's damage is disputed, and the client sides with yes. Icy Veins says pets "do not have an inherent damage buff or reduction based on type." Three sources say otherwise. foreverchanges.pro's reading of the client keeps Classic's family table. Wowhead writes that Cats and Raptors "have a 1.1x damage modifier." WoWSims fitted a level 30 Cat's logged swings with that same 10% (WoWSims' model). The client's figures, measured against a beast of no family:

So a Bear's SwipeSwipeLevel 12 · Spell · Physical · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost20 FocusRangeMeleeCooldown5 sec cooldownSwipe 3 nearby enemies, inflicting 4 damage. costs about a tenth of the pet's damage against a Cat, and buys Health and Armor. Foxes are new to Forever.

Attack speed belongs to the beast you tame. Every pet swings every 2.0 seconds, and a passive the beast brings with it changes that. Blizzard's notes say untraining a pet no longer strips the passive.

What changed from Classic

Pets get increased stats from your gearBlizzard publishes no coefficients for it. A pet can no longer be stat-buffed directly: Blizzard confirms pets cannot receive player buffs that increase their stats, so gear the Hunter, not the pet

At level 60

The three trees end in different places, and the spec pages print the published level 60 builds.

  • Beast Mastery takes 31 points to Bestial WrathBestial WrathTalentCastInstantCost12% of base ManaRange100 yd rangeCooldown120 sec cooldownDuration18 secSend your pet into a rage causing 50% additional damage for 18 sec. While enraged, the beast does not feel pity or remorse or fear and it cannot be stopped unless killed. and the rest in Marksmanship for Lethal AttacksLethal AttacksTalent · Rank 5 of 5CastInstantIncreases your critical strike chance with all attacks by 5%. and Careful AimCareful AimTalent · Rank 5 of 5CastInstantIncreases your Attack Power by 100% of your Intellect..
  • Marksmanship has two shapes: with Lone WolfLone WolfTalentCastInstantYou deal 20% increased damage with all attacks while you do not have an active pet. and no pet, or with a pet and a Beast Mastery second tree. Icy Veins prints both.
  • Survival has three: full melee, weaving in and out, or ranged. Wowhead prints the first two and WoWSims models all three (WoWSims' model).

The two sites disagree on the hit you need at 60. Wowhead says 9%, Icy Veins 8%.

In a dungeon the pet is not the tank and you out-threaten it on several targets. All enemies within 10 yards will be slowed by 60% while in the area of effect. Trap will exist for 60 sec.
